run.question:
Alertmanager alert HighRequestLatency (severity critical) is firing for service otel-demo/frontend-proxy since 2026-11-25T20:12:33Z.
Investigate why this alert is firing.

report.summary: The HighRequestLatency alert for otel-demo/frontend-proxy is firing because a Kubernetes NetworkPolicy named frontend-ingress (namespace otel-demo) was created at 2026-11-25T20:11:37Z with policyTypes [Ingress] and no ingress rules, i.e. a default-deny on all ingress to the frontend pods. In the same second the frontend stopped serving traffic (its last application log line is a 200 at 20:11:37.562Z and it then stops producing spans), while frontend-proxy's own spans show its upstream calls to frontend hanging ~5.0s and failing with HTTP 503 / error status. frontend-proxy p95 rose from ~34 ms (20:08-20:12) to 3778 ms at 20:13:00, 6119 ms at 20:14:00 and 7422 ms at 20:15:00, which is the value the alert reports. The same deny-all ingress plausibly explains the second, pending HighRequestLatency alert for service agent (14201 ms): the agent's APPLICATION_ENDPOINT is frontend:8080 and its sampled tool-call spans (execute_tool list_products, execute_task tools, LangGraph workflow) take ~10.0-10.1 s, while its model spans ChatLLM.chat stay at 24-36 ms and POST /prompt returns 200. No pod restarted, no deployment/image/ConfigMap changed after the initial 20:04 rollout, and the frontend container is still running with restartCount 0, so a pod crash, OOM, rollout or flagd-based fault is not supported by the objects and logs read. The only object change observed near the onset is the NetworkPolicy, and the cluster runs Cilium, which enforces NetworkPolicy. Not verified: who/what created the policy (only field manager OpenAPI-Generator is visible; no change-history integration), and Cilium's enforcement verdicts, which were not readable.

claims.text: The rule opentelemetrydemo.backend.goldensignal/HighRequestLatency evaluates histogram_quantile(0.95, sum by (le, service_name, namespace) (rate(traces_span_metrics_duration_milliseconds_bucket{namespace="otel-demo",service_name!~"flagd|load-generator|frontend*"}[2m]))) > 1500 and is firing for service_name=frontend-proxy since 2026-11-25T20:12:33Z with value 7522.727272727268; the same rule has a pending alert for service_name=agent since 20:13:03Z with value 14201.388888888887. A second rule, opentelemetrydemo.frontend.goldensignal/HighRequestLatency (service_name=~"frontend|frontend-proxy"), is pending for frontend-proxy with 7490.384615384613.

frontend-proxy p95 (histogram_quantile over traces_span_metrics_duration_milliseconds_bucket, 2m rate) was ~34-37 ms at 20:08:00-20:12:00 and then jumped to 3778.3 ms at 20:13:00, 6119.97 ms at 20:14:00 and 7422.3 ms at 20:15:00; frontend p95 stayed at ~31-35 ms through 20:14:00 and returned NaN at 20:15:00; agent p95 was 199-362 ms through 20:12:00 and then 13841.3 ms at 20:14:00 and 14129.6 ms at 20:15:00.

At 20:15:30 the 3m p95 by service was 7422.3 ms for frontend-proxy, 14129.6 ms for agent, NaN for frontend, and ~1.9 ms for cart, flagd, ad and image-provider; span rates summed over all status codes were 5.09/s (STATUS_CODE_ERROR) and 5.09/s (STATUS_CODE_UNSET) for frontend-proxy, 5.15/s error for load-generator, and 0 for frontend.

frontend-proxy spans in the incident window show 20 GET server spans with error=true, http.status_code=503, otel.status_code=ERROR and 9 POST server spans likewise, with durations up to 5.00 s (e.g. span 588ead4a26918012 GET 5002492 us, span 137d08d87aa3f784 POST 5001974 us); the matching child spans 'router frontend egress' (service frontend-proxy, span_kind client) carry error="true", http.status_code="0" and nearly identical durations (e.g. span 0d0502fc3fd8be4c 5002295 us), and load-generator client spans for the same calls also end in 503.

frontend-proxy error span rate (traces_span_metrics_calls_total, status_code STATUS_CODE_ERROR) was 0/s until 20:12:30 and then 7.66/s at 20:13:00, 12.37/s at 20:14:00 and 13.07/s at 20:15:00, while frontend's span rate fell to 0 from 20:13:30 onward (last non-zero reading 52.7/s at 20:13:00).

The frontend pod frontend-5c847cc9bd-hvfzl (namespace otel-demo, pod IP 10.244.2.234) is phase Running, all conditions True, container frontend ready=true with restartCount 0, lastState empty, startedAt 2026-11-25T20:04:11Z; its fetched logs contain only successful 'API request completed' 200 lines and end at 2026-11-25T20:11:37.562729Z, with no previous container instance available.

NetworkPolicy otel-demo/frontend-ingress has creationTimestamp 2026-11-25T20:11:37Z, field manager 'OpenAPI-Generator' (operation Update, time 2026-11-25T20:11:37Z), podSelector matchLabels {app.kubernetes.io/component: frontend, app.kubernetes.io/name: frontend, app.kubernetes.io/version: 3.1.0, opentelemetry.io/name: frontend}, policyTypes ["Ingress"] and no ingress rules, i.e. it denies all ingress to the selected frontend pods.

frontend-ingress is the only NetworkPolicy in namespace otel-demo, and the cluster's kube-system namespace runs Cilium agent pods (cilium-4prsl, cilium-t5477, cilium-zf69j and cilium-envoy-*), a CNI that enforces NetworkPolicy.

Nothing was rolled out during the window: every otel-demo pod was created at 20:04:10-20:04:14 with restartCount 0, all 26 otel-demo Deployments are at generation 1 with last field-manager write at 20:04:13-20:04:26Z (frontend 20:04:14Z, frontend-proxy 20:04:15Z), and all otel-demo ConfigMaps were last written at 20:04:06-20:04:10Z.

The frontend Deployment's container has no readinessProbe or livenessProbe and only a 250Mi memory limit/request, image ghcr.io/open-telemetry/demo:3.1.0-frontend; the frontend Service endpoint is present with 10.244.2.234:8080, so the pod is registered as ready and it is a network-level block, not endpoint removal, that can cut its ingress.

The agent Deployment sets APPLICATION_ENDPOINT=frontend:8080 (same in mcp), and sampled agent traces between 20:12:30 and 20:15:45 show 10.0-10.1 s spans on execute_tool list_products (10047401 us, 10045757 us, 10046849 us), execute_task tools and LangGraph.workflow, while ChatLLM.chat spans are 24-36 ms and POST /prompt spans return http.status_code=200; frontend-tool spans are therefore the slow part of the agent request.

otel-demo events between 20:04:10Z and 20:04:26Z contain only Scheduling/Pulling/Pulled/Created/Started/ScalingReplicaSet/SuccessfulCreate entries plus one Warning Unhealthy on otel-collector-74d749ff5f-xs6m4 at 20:04:11Z for a connection-refused readiness probe; no event names an Evicted, OOMKilled, BackOff or Failed condition for frontend or frontend-proxy, and no event mentions a NetworkPolicy.

The flagd ConfigMap demo.flagd.json loaded by the flagd pod (logs show the file synced at 20:04:12Z and no later flagd activity) sets every fault flag defaultVariant to "off", including imageSlowLoad, aiSlowResponse and aiRunawayAgent; no flagd log in the fetched stream records a flag change.

The frontend-ingress NetworkPolicy (created 20:11:37Z, Ingress-type with no rules) is what cut all traffic to the frontend pods: from that second the frontend logged nothing and emitted no spans, frontend-proxy's client spans to the frontend hung ~5.0 s and returned 503, and the agent's calls to frontend:8080 hung ~10.0 s. The exact second-level coincidence of policy creation, last frontend request log and the start of proxy 503s, plus Cilium enforcement, makes this the deepest supported cause.

The pending HighRequestLatency alert for service agent has the same cause: the agent's tools call APPLICATION_ENDPOINT frontend:8080, so frontend ingress being denied turns its tool calls into ~10 s waits and lifts its p95 to ~14 s while its model calls and POST /prompt responses remain normal.

The policy was applied by an out-of-band client rather than by the Helm release: the object carries opentelemetry-demo-0.42.8 Helm labels but its only field manager is 'OpenAPI-Generator' at 20:11:37Z, seven minutes after the helm Apply of all workloads at 20:04:10Z, which is the pattern of a programmatic fault injection.

The frontend is not itself crashing or misconfigured at the process level: its pod is Running and Ready with restartCount 0 and lastState empty, all log lines before 20:11:37 are 200 responses, and the pod has no probe that could have marked it unready, so its 'Ready' state neither contradicts nor explains the loss of traffic.

Pod crash, OOMKill or eviction on frontend or frontend-proxy is rejected: restartCount is 0 for every otel-demo pod including frontend-5c847cc9bd-hvfzl and frontend-proxy-77df9b8f7-rmbrg, the frontend container's lastState is empty, and otel-demo events contain no Evicted, OOMKilled, BackOff or Failed reason.

A rollout, image change or configuration edit of frontend or frontend-proxy is rejected as the trigger: all otel-demo Deployments are at generation 1 with last writes at 20:04:13-20:04:26Z, all pods date from 20:04:10-20:04:14Z with a single ReplicaSet create per Deployment, and every otel-demo ConfigMap was last written by 20:04:10Z, well before the 20:11:37Z onset.

A flagd feature-flag fault (for example imageSlowLoad or aiSlowResponse) is not supported by what was read: every flag in the flagd-config demo.flagd.json is defaultVariant "off", the flagd file sync completed at 20:04:12Z and the fetched flagd/flagd-ui log stream ends at 20:04:16Z with no change recorded; runtime flag evaluation state could not be read directly.

Check Cilium/Hubble policy verdicts for the frontend pods around 2026-11-25T20:11:37Z and identify the principal behind field manager 'OpenAPI-Generator' that created otel-demo/frontend-ingress; if the deny-all ingress is not intended, removing or correcting that NetworkPolicy (for example by allowing ingress from frontend-proxy on 8080) is the corrective action to evaluate, and the frontend, frontend-proxy, agent and load-generator signals should be re-checked afterwards.

gaps: The change_history integration is not available in this Run, so who or what created otel-demo/frontend-ingress (beyond the field manager name 'OpenAPI-Generator') and whether it was the intended injected fault cannot be confirmed.

Cilium policy verdicts / Hubble flows and the frontend pod's network are not readable with the available tools, so enforcement is inferred from the Cilium agent pods plus the second-level timing coincidence and the observed traffic cutoff, not from packet-level evidence.

traces_search for service frontend in 2026-11-25T20:11:40Z-20:15:45Z returned no_data (only that this query matched nothing), so the absence of frontend spans after 20:11:40Z rests on the traces_span_metrics calls/p95 readings and on the log stream ending at 20:11:37.562Z, not on a sampled trace view.

Whether the agent's ~14.2 s alert value is fully explained by its ~10.0 s frontend tool calls could not be verified from the sampled traces; traces are a biased sample and trace span counts are not request counts, so the agent-side impact magnitude remains approximate.
flagd runtime flag evaluation state (as opposed to the ConfigMap file content, which shows all flags off) could not be queried; the mcp service's own latency/errors were not individually checked.
next_steps: Query Cilium/Hubble flow and policy verdict data for the frontend pod IP 10.244.2.234 around 2026-11-25T20:11:37Z to confirm ingress drops from frontend-proxy (10.244.2.92) and agent (10.244.2.225).
Review audit logs for the principal using the OpenAPI-Generator field manager that created otel-demo/frontend-ingress at 2026-11-25T20:11:37Z.
Decide whether frontend-ingress should allow ingress from frontend-proxy (and the agent) on port 8080, and validate frontend request logs and frontend-proxy 503 rate after the policy is corrected.
If flagd-based faults are suspected, read flagd's runtime flag evaluation state rather than only the mounted demo.flagd.json.
